2.11.3 Module Patterns

// Configuration module (config/index.js)
export const config = {
    apiUrl: process.env.REACT_APP_API_URL || 'http://localhost:3000',
    timeout: 5000,
    retryAttempts: 3
};

// Service module (services/auth.js)
const TOKEN_KEY = 'auth_token';

export const AuthService = {
    login: async (credentials) => {
        try {
            const response = await fetch(`${config.apiUrl}/auth/login`, {
                method: 'POST',
                headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
                body: JSON.stringify(credentials)
            });

            if (!response.ok) {
                throw new Error('Login failed');
            }

            const data = await response.json();
            localStorage.setItem(TOKEN_KEY, data.token);
            return data;
        } catch (error) {
            console.error('Login error:', error);
            throw error;
        }
    },

    logout: () => {
        localStorage.removeItem(TOKEN_KEY);
    },

    getToken: () => localStorage.getItem(TOKEN_KEY),

    isAuthenticated: () => !!localStorage.getItem(TOKEN_KEY)
};

// Constants module (constants/index.js)
export const ROUTES = {
    HOME: '/',
    LOGIN: '/login',
    DASHBOARD: '/dashboard',
    USERS: '/users',
    SETTINGS: '/settings'
};

export const API = {
    USERS: '/api/users',
    AUTH: '/api/auth',
    POSTS: '/api/posts'
};

// Utility module (utils/formatters.js)
export const formatters = {
    formatDate: (date) => {
        return new Date(date).toLocaleDateString('en-US', {
            year: 'numeric',
            month: 'long',
            day: 'numeric'
        });
    },

    formatCurrency: (amount) => {
        return new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', {
            style: 'currency',
            currency: 'USD'
        }).format(amount);
    },

    formatPhone: (phone) => {
        return phone.replace(/(\d{3})(\d{3})(\d{4})/, '($1) $2-$3');
    }
};

// API module with error handling (api/client.js)
import { AuthService } from '../services/auth';
import { config } from '../config';

export const apiClient = {
    async request(endpoint, options = {}) {
        const token = AuthService.getToken();
        const headers = {
            'Content-Type': 'application/json',
            ...(token && { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}` }),
            ...options.headers
        };

        try {
            const response = await fetch(`${config.apiUrl}${endpoint}`, {
                ...options,
                headers
            });

            if (!response.ok) {
                throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}: ${response.statusText}`);
            }

            return await response.json();
        } catch (error) {
            console.error('API request error:', error);
            throw error;
        }
    },

    get: (endpoint) => this.request(endpoint),
    post: (endpoint, data) => this.request(endpoint, { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(data) }),
    put: (endpoint, data) => this.request(endpoint, { method: 'PUT', body: JSON.stringify(data) }),
    delete: (endpoint) => this.request(endpoint, { method: 'DELETE' })
};

2.12 Closures

2.12.1 Understanding Closures

// Basic closure
function outerFunction(outerVariable) {
    // Inner function has access to outerVariable
    function innerFunction(innerVariable) {
        return outerVariable + innerVariable;
    }
    return innerFunction;
}

const closure = outerFunction(10);
console.log(closure(5)); // 15

// Closures in React
function Counter() {
    // Closure captures state and handlers
    const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

    const increment = () => {
        setCount(prev => prev + 1);
    };

    const decrement = () => {
        setCount(prev => prev - 1);
    };

    // These functions form closures around count and setCount
    return (
        <div>
            <p>Count: {count}</p>
            <button onClick={increment}>+</button>
            <button onClick={decrement}>-</button>
        </div>
    );
}

// Closure for private variables
function createCounter() {
    let count = 0; // Private variable

    return {
        increment: function() {
            count++;
            return count;
        },
        decrement: function() {
            count--;
            return count;
        },
        getValue: function() {
            return count;
        }
    };
}

const counter = createCounter();
console.log(counter.increment()); // 1
console.log(counter.increment()); // 2
console.log(counter.getValue()); // 2
// console.log(counter.count); // undefined (private)

2.12.2 Closure in React Hooks

// UseState uses closures
function ComponentWithClosure() {
    const [value, setValue] = useState(0);

    // This handler forms a closure around value
    const handleClick = () => {
        setValue(value + 1);
    };

    // This handler captures the current value
    const handleLog = () => {
        console.log('Current value:', value);
    };

    return (
        <div>
            <p>Value: {value}</p>
            <button onClick={handleClick}>Increment</button>
            <button onClick={handleLog}>Log Value</button>
        </div>
    );
}

// Closure with useEffect - stale closure problem
function StaleClosure() {
    const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

    useEffect(() => {
        // This closure captures the initial count (0)
        const interval = setInterval(() => {
            console.log('Count:', count); // Always logs initial count
        }, 1000);

        return () => clearInterval(interval);
    }, []); // Empty dependency array

    return <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Increment</button>;
}

// Fixing stale closure
function FixedClosure() {
    const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

    useEffect(() => {
        // Use functional update to get current value
        const interval = setInterval(() => {
            setCount(prev => {
                console.log('Count:', prev);
                return prev;
            });
        }, 1000);

        return () => clearInterval(interval);
    }, []);

    return <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Increment</button>;
}

// Closures in custom hooks
function useCounter(initialValue = 0) {
    const [count, setCount] = useState(initialValue);

    // These functions close over count and setCount
    const increment = useCallback(() => {
        setCount(c => c + 1);
    }, []);

    const decrement = useCallback(() => {
        setCount(c => c - 1);
    }, []);

    const reset = useCallback(() => {
        setCount(initialValue);
    }, [initialValue]);

    return { count, increment, decrement, reset };
}

2.13 Event Loop and Execution Context

2.13.1 Understanding the Event Loop

// Visualizing the event loop
console.log('1: Start');

setTimeout(() => {
    console.log('2: Timeout callback');
}, 0);

Promise.resolve().then(() => {
    console.log('3: Promise resolved');
});

console.log('4: End');

// Output:
// 1: Start
// 4: End
// 3: Promise resolved
// 2: Timeout callback

// Event Loop Phases
// 1. Call Stack - Synchronous code
// 2. Microtasks - Promises, process.nextTick
// 3. Macrotasks - setTimeout, setInterval, I/O

// Microtask vs Macrotask priority
setTimeout(() => {
    console.log('Macrotask');
}, 0);

Promise.resolve().then(() => {
    console.log('Microtask 1');
}).then(() => {
    console.log('Microtask 2');
});

// Output:
// Microtask 1
// Microtask 2
// Macrotask

// Event loop in React
function EventLoopExample() {
    const [data, setData] = useState(null);

    useEffect(() => {
        console.log('1: Effect start');

        // Async operation - scheduled in event loop
        fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
            .then(response => {
                console.log('3: Promise resolved');
                return response.json();
            })
            .then(json => {
                console.log('4: Data processed');
                setData(json);
            });

        console.log('2: Effect end');

        // Output order:
        // 1: Effect start
        // 2: Effect end
        // 3: Promise resolved
        // 4: Data processed
    }, []);

    return <div>{data}</div>;
}

2.13.2 Execution Context and This

// Execution Context
function example() {
    // Function execution context
    let x = 10;

    function inner() {
        // Inner execution context
        let y = 20;
        console.log(x + y); // 30 (accesses outer scope)
    }

    inner();
}

// 'this' binding
// 1. Default binding (global)
function showThis() {
    console.log(this); // global object (window in browser)
}

// 2. Implicit binding (object method)
const obj = {
    name: 'John',
    greet: function() {
        console.log(`Hello, ${this.name}`);
    }
};
obj.greet(); // Hello, John

// 3. Explicit binding (call, apply, bind)
function greet(greeting) {
    console.log(`${greeting}, ${this.name}`);
}

const person = { name: 'Jane' };
greet.call(person, 'Hello'); // Hello, Jane
greet.apply(person, ['Hi']); // Hi, Jane
const boundGreet = greet.bind(person, 'Hey');
boundGreet(); // Hey, Jane

// 4. Arrow function binding (lexical)
const arrowObj = {
    name: 'Bob',
    greet: () => {
        console.log(`Hello, ${this.name}`); // this refers to outer scope
    }
};
arrowObj.greet(); // Hello, undefined (if global)

// 'this' in React
class ReactComponent extends React.Component {
    constructor(props) {
        super(props);
        this.state = { count: 0 };
        this.handleClick = this.handleClick.bind(this); // Manual binding
    }

    // Arrow function - automatically bound
    handleClickArrow = () => {
        this.setState({ count: this.state.count + 1 });
    };

    // Regular function - needs binding
    handleClick() {
        this.setState({ count: this.state.count + 1 });
    }

    render() {
        return (
            <div>
                <button onClick={this.handleClick}>Count: {this.state.count}</button>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

2.14 Memory and Garbage Collection

2.14.1 Memory Management

// Memory allocation
let number = 10; // Allocates memory for number
let string = 'Hello'; // Allocates memory for string
let object = { name: 'John' }; // Allocates memory for object
let array = [1, 2, 3]; // Allocates memory for array

// Memory references
let user = { name: 'John' };
let userRef = user; // Both reference the same object
userRef.name = 'Jane';
console.log(user.name); // 'Jane' (same object)

// Memory cleanup with closures
function createClosure() {
    let largeData = new Array(1000000).fill('data');

    return function() {
        console.log(largeData.length);
    };
}

// The closure holds reference to largeData
const closure = createClosure();
// Memory for largeData is not freed until closure is garbage collected

// React: Cleanup with useEffect
function MemoryLeakExample() {
    useEffect(() => {
        // Subscriptions, event listeners
        const subscription = someEventSource.subscribe();
        const handler = () => console.log('Event');
        window.addEventListener('resize', handler);

        // Cleanup - prevents memory leaks
        return () => {
            subscription.unsubscribe();
            window.removeEventListener('resize', handler);
        };
    }, []);

    return <div>Memory Leak Example</div>;
}

// Avoiding memory leaks with useRef
function ImageLoader({ src }) {
    const [image, setImage] = useState(null);
    const abortController = useRef(null);

    useEffect(() => {
        // Create new AbortController for each request
        abortController.current = new AbortController();

        fetch(src, { signal: abortController.current.signal })
            .then(response => response.blob())
            .then(blob => {
                const imageUrl = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
                setImage(imageUrl);
            })
            .catch(error => {
                if (error.name !== 'AbortError') {
                    console.error('Error loading image:', error);
                }
            });

        // Cleanup
        return () => {
            abortController.current.abort();
            if (image) {
                URL.revokeObjectURL(image); // Clean up URL
            }
        };
    }, [src]);

    return image ? <img src={image} alt="Loaded" /> : <div>Loading...</div>;
}

2.14.2 Garbage Collection

// Garbage collection basics
function createObject() {
    let obj = { data: 'some data' };
    return obj;
}

// Object is eligible for garbage collection when no references exist
let myObj = createObject();
myObj = null; // Object can be garbage collected now

// Garbage collection in React components
function ComponentWithLargeData() {
    const [data, setData] = useState(null);

    useEffect(() => {
        let largeData = new Array(1000000);
        setData(largeData);

        // When component unmounts, data will be garbage collected
        // if no other references exist
    }, []);

    return <div>Component</div>;
}

// WeakMap and WeakSet - allow garbage collection
let weakMap = new WeakMap();
let obj = {};
weakMap.set(obj, 'some data');
obj = null; // obj can be garbage collected

// WeakRef - weak reference to object
let weakRef = new WeakRef({ data: 'data' });
// Use deref to get the object
let objRef = weakRef.deref();
if (objRef) {
    console.log(objRef.data);
}

// Memory leak detection in React
function useLeakDetection(componentName) {
    useEffect(() => {
        console.log(`${componentName} mounted`);
        return () => {
            console.log(`${componentName} unmounted`);
            // Check for leaks
            if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
                // Check for event listeners
                // Check for subscriptions
                // Check for references
            }
        };
    }, [componentName]);
}

// Using the hook
function MyComponent() {
    useLeakDetection('MyComponent');
    return <div>My Component</div>;
}

2.15 ES6+ Features for React

2.15.1 Template Literals

// Basic template literals
const name = 'John';
const age = 30;
const greeting = `Hello, ${name}! You are ${age} years old.`;

// Multi-line strings
const html = `
    <div class="user-card">
        <h2>${name}</h2>
        <p>Age: ${age}</p>
    </div>
`;

// Expression evaluation
const price = 100;
const tax = 0.08;
const total = `Total: $${price * (1 + tax)}`;

// Tagged template literals
function highlight(strings, ...values) {
    return strings.reduce((result, str, i) => {
        return result + str + (values[i] ? `<strong>${values[i]}</strong>` : '');
    }, '');
}

const highlighted = highlight`Hello ${name}, your total is $${total}`;

// React: Template literals in CSS
function StyledComponent() {
    const theme = 'dark';
    const styles = `
        .container {
            background: ${theme === 'dark' ? '#333' : '#fff'};
            color: ${theme === 'dark' ? '#fff' : '#333'};
        }
    `;

    return <div className="container">Content</div>;
}

2.15.2 Optional Chaining (?.)

// Accessing nested properties safely
const user = {
    name: 'John',
    address: {
        city: 'New York',
        street: '5th Ave'
    }
};

// Without optional chaining
const city = user && user.address && user.address.city;

// With optional chaining
const city = user?.address?.city;

// Optional chaining with arrays
const users = [
    { name: 'John' },
    { name: 'Jane' }
];
const firstUserName = users[0]?.name;

// Optional chaining with function calls
const result = user.getFullName?.();

// React: Optional chaining in components
function UserProfile({ user }) {
    return (
        <div>
            <h2>{user?.name ?? 'Unknown'}</h2>
            <p>{user?.address?.city ?? 'No city'}</p>
            <p>Email: {user?.email || 'Not provided'}</p>
            <span>Phone: {user?.phone?.number || 'N/A'}</span>
        </div>
    );
}

2.15.3 Nullish Coalescing (??)

// Nullish coalescing - only works for null or undefined
const value = null ?? 'default';
console.log(value); // 'default'

const value2 = undefined ?? 'default';
console.log(value2); // 'default'

const value3 = 0 ?? 'default';
console.log(value3); // 0

const value4 = '' ?? 'default';
console.log(value4); // ''

// Difference from || operator
const zero = 0 || 'default';
console.log(zero); // 'default' (0 is falsy)

const zero2 = 0 ?? 'default';
console.log(zero2); // 0 (0 is not null or undefined)

// React: Nullish coalescing
function Component({ data, settings }) {
    const count = data?.count ?? 0;
    const theme = settings?.theme ?? 'light';
    const language = settings?.language ?? 'en';

    return (
        <div>
            <p>Count: {count}</p>
            <p>Theme: {theme}</p>
            <p>Language: {language}</p>
        </div>
    );
}

// Combining with optional chaining
const result = user?.preferences?.theme ?? 'default-theme';

2.16 Classes and Prototypes

2.16.1 Class Basics

// Class declaration
class User {
    // Constructor
    constructor(name, email) {
        this.name = name;
        this.email = email;
        this.createdAt = new Date();
    }

    // Instance method
    getInfo() {
        return `${this.name} (${this.email})`;
    }

    // Static method
    static createGuest() {
        return new User('Guest', 'guest@example.com');
    }

    // Getter
    get emailDomain() {
        return this.email.split('@')[1];
    }

    // Setter
    set emailDomain(domain) {
        const username = this.email.split('@')[0];
        this.email = `${username}@${domain}`;
    }
}

// Class inheritance
class AdminUser extends User {
    constructor(name, email, permissions) {
        super(name, email); // Call parent constructor
        this.permissions = permissions || ['read', 'write'];
        this.isAdmin = true;
    }

    // Override method
    getInfo() {
        return `Admin: ${super.getInfo()}`;
    }

    // New method
    hasPermission(permission) {
        return this.permissions.includes(permission);
    }
}

// Using classes
const user = new User('John', 'john@example.com');
console.log(user.getInfo()); // John (john@example.com)
console.log(user.emailDomain); // example.com

const admin = new AdminUser('Jane', 'jane@example.com', ['read', 'write', 'delete']);
console.log(admin.getInfo()); // Admin: Jane (jane@example.com)
console.log(admin.hasPermission('delete')); // true

2.16.2 Prototypes and Prototype Chain

// Understanding prototypes
function Animal(name) {
    this.name = name;
}

Animal.prototype.speak = function() {
    console.log(`${this.name} makes a sound`);
};

const dog = new Animal('Dog');
dog.speak(); // Dog makes a sound

// Prototype chain
console.log(dog.__proto__ === Animal.prototype); // true
console.log(Animal.prototype.__proto__ === Object.prototype); // true
console.log(Object.prototype.__proto__ === null); // true

// Class-based prototype inheritance
class Animal {
    constructor(name) {
        this.name = name;
    }

    speak() {
        console.log(`${this.name} makes a sound`);
    }
}

class Dog extends Animal {
    speak() {
        console.log(`${this.name} barks`);
    }
}

const dog = new Dog('Rex');
dog.speak(); // Rex barks

// React: Using classes for components (legacy)
class Welcome extends React.Component {
    constructor(props) {
        super(props);
        this.state = { count: 0 };
    }

    componentDidMount() {
        console.log('Component mounted');
    }

    render() {
        return <h1>Hello, {this.props.name}</h1>;
    }
}

// Modern approach with functional components and hooks
function Welcome({ name }) {
    const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

    useEffect(() => {
        console.log('Component mounted');
    }, []);

    return <h1>Hello, {name}</h1>;
}

2.17 Practical React JavaScript Examples

2.17.1 Creating a Custom Hook with JavaScript

// Custom hook using all JavaScript features
function useFetchData(url, options = {}) {
    const [data, setData] = useState(null);
    const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
    const [error, setError] = useState(null);

    useEffect(() => {
        const abortController = new AbortController();

        const fetchData = async () => {
            try {
                setLoading(true);
                setError(null);

                const response = await fetch(url, {
                    ...options,
                    signal: abortController.signal
                });

                if (!response.ok) {
                    throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
                }

                const result = await response.json();
                setData(result);
            } catch (err) {
                if (err.name !== 'AbortError') {
                    setError(err.message);
                }
            } finally {
                setLoading(false);
            }
        };

        fetchData();

        return () => {
            abortController.abort();
        };
    }, [url, JSON.stringify(options)]);

    return { data, loading, error };
}

// Using the custom hook
function UserList() {
    const { data: users, loading, error } = useFetchData('/api/users');

    if (loading) return <Spinner />;
    if (error) return <ErrorDisplay error={error} />;

    return (
        <ul>
            {users?.map(user => (
                <li key={user.id}>
                    {user.name} - {user.email}
                </li>
            ))}
        </ul>
    );
}

2.17.2 Data Transformation Patterns

// Complex data transformation
const rawData = {
    users: [
        { id: 1, name: 'John Doe', email: 'john@example.com', status: 'active' },
        { id: 2, name: 'Jane Smith', email: 'jane@example.com', status: 'inactive' },
        { id: 3, name: 'Bob Johnson', email: 'bob@example.com', status: 'active' }
    ],
    posts: [
        { id: 1, userId: 1, title: 'First Post', content: 'Content 1' },
        { id: 2, userId: 1, title: 'Second Post', content: 'Content 2' },
        { id: 3, userId: 2, title: 'Third Post', content: 'Content 3' }
    ]
};

// Transform data for UI
const transformedData = {
    // Group users by status
    usersByStatus: rawData.users.reduce((acc, user) => {
        if (!acc[user.status]) acc[user.status] = [];
        acc[user.status].push(user);
        return acc;
    }, {}),

    // Map users to their posts
    userPosts: rawData.users.map(user => ({
        ...user,
        posts: rawData.posts.filter(post => post.userId === user.id)
    })),

    // Create name-email map
    userEmailMap: rawData.users.reduce((acc, user) => {
        acc[user.id] = { name: user.name, email: user.email };
        return acc;
    }, {}),

    // Find active users with posts
    activeUsersWithPosts: rawData.users
        .filter(user => user.status === 'active')
        .map(user => ({
            ...user,
            postCount: rawData.posts.filter(post => post.userId === user.id).length
        }))
};

// React component using transformed data
function Dashboard({ data }) {
    const { usersByStatus, userPosts, activeUsersWithPosts } = data;

    return (
        <div>
            <div className="stats">
                {Object.entries(usersByStatus).map(([status, users]) => (
                    <div key={status}>
                        <h3>{status.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + status.slice(1)}</h3>
                        <p>Count: {users.length}</p>
                    </div>
                ))}
            </div>

            <div className="user-posts">
                {userPosts.map(user => (
                    <div key={user.id} className="user-card">
                        <h3>{user.name}</h3>
                        <p>{user.email}</p>
                        <ul>
                            {user.posts.map(post => (
                                <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
                            ))}
                        </ul>
                    </div>
                ))}
            </div>
        </div>
    );
}

2.18 Common Mistakes and Best Practices

2.18.1 Common JavaScript Mistakes in React

// ❌ Mutating state directly
function BadComponent() {
    const [items, setItems] = useState([1, 2, 3]);

    const addItem = (item) => {
        items.push(item); // Direct mutation
        setItems(items); // Wrong - same reference
    };
}

// ✅ Proper state update
function GoodComponent() {
    const [items, setItems] = useState([1, 2, 3]);

    const addItem = (item) => {
        setItems(prev => [...prev, item]); // New array reference
    };
}

// ❌ Using var
var oldStyle = 'This is legacy';
// var is function-scoped and can lead to bugs

// ✅ Using let and const
let newStyle = 'Modern JavaScript';
const constantStyle = 'Cannot be reassigned';

// ❌ Incorrect 'this' binding
class BadClass extends React.Component {
    handleClick() {
        console.log(this); // 'this' is undefined
    }
}

// ✅ Proper 'this' binding
class GoodClass extends React.Component {
    handleClick = () => {
        console.log(this); // 'this' is properly bound
    };
}

// ❌ Not handling async errors
async function badFetch() {
    const data = await fetch('/api/data').then(r => r.json());
    return data; // If fetch fails, error goes unhandled
}

// ✅ Proper error handling
async function goodFetch() {
    try {
        const response = await fetch('/api/data');
        if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Failed to fetch');
        return await response.json();
    } catch (error) {
        console.error('Fetch error:', error);
        throw error; // Or handle appropriately
    }
}

// ❌ Memory leak in useEffect
function BadEffect() {
    useEffect(() => {
        const handler = () => console.log('resize');
        window.addEventListener('resize', handler);
        // Missing cleanup
    }, []);
}

// ✅ Proper cleanup
function GoodEffect() {
    useEffect(() => {
        const handler = () => console.log('resize');
        window.addEventListener('resize', handler);
        return () => {
            window.removeEventListener('resize', handler);
        };
    }, []);
}

2.18.2 Best Practices

// ✅ Use descriptive variable names
// Bad: const d = new Date();
// Good: const currentDate = new Date();

// ✅ Use const by default, let when needed
const API_URL = 'https://api.example.com';
let counter = 0; // Only if you need to reassign

// ✅ Use destructuring for props
function Component({ user, onUpdate, onDelete }) {
    // Instead of props.user, props.onUpdate
}

// ✅ Use spread operator for immutability
const updatedState = {
    ...state,
    property: newValue
};

// ✅ Use template literals
const message = `Hello, ${name}! You have ${count} messages.`;

// ✅ Use optional chaining
const city = user?.address?.city ?? 'Unknown';

// ✅ Use array methods for transformations
const activeUsers = users
    .filter(user => user.active)
    .map(user => user.name);

// ✅ Use async/await for promises
async function fetchData() {
    try {
        const response = await fetch('/api/data');
        return await response.json();
    } catch (error) {
        console.error('Error:', error);
        throw error;
    }
}

// ✅ Use custom hooks for reusable logic
function useLocalStorage(key, initialValue) {
    const [value, setValue] = useState(() => {
        try {
            const item = localStorage.getItem(key);
            return item ? JSON.parse(item) : initialValue;
        } catch (error) {
            return initialValue;
        }
    });

    useEffect(() => {
        try {
            localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(value));
        } catch (error) {
            console.error('Error saving to localStorage:', error);
        }
    }, [key, value]);

    return [value, setValue];
}

2.19 Interview Questions

Junior Level Questions

Q: What's the difference between let, const, and var?

Answer: - var: Function-scoped, can be redeclared, hoisted with undefined - let: Block-scoped, cannot be redeclared, hoisted but not initialized - const: Block-scoped, cannot be reassigned, hoisted but not initialized

console.log(x); // undefined
var x = 1;

// console.log(y); // ReferenceError
let y = 2;

// console.log(z); // ReferenceError
const z = 3;

Q: What is the difference between == and ===?

Answer: - ==: Loose equality, performs type coercion - ===: Strict equality, checks both value and type

console.log(5 == '5'); // true (string converted to number)
console.log(5 === '5'); // false (different types)
console.log(null == undefined); // true
console.log(null === undefined); // false

Mid Level Questions

Q: Explain arrow functions and their advantages.

Answer: Arrow functions provide a shorter syntax and lexical this binding. They don't have their own this, arguments, super, or new.target.

// Shorter syntax
const add = (a, b) => a + b;

// Lexical 'this'
const obj = {
    name: 'John',
    greet: function() {
        setTimeout(() => {
            console.log(`Hello, ${this.name}`); // 'this' refers to obj
        }, 1000);
    }
};

Q: What are closures and how are they used in React?

Answer: Closures are functions that have access to variables from their outer scope. In React, closures are fundamental to hooks and callbacks.

function Counter() {
    const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

    // This function forms a closure over count
    const handleClick = () => {
        setCount(count + 1); // Uses closure to access count
    };

    return <button onClick={handleClick}>{count}</button>;
}

Senior Level Questions

Q: Explain the event loop and how it affects React performance.

Answer: The event loop handles asynchronous operations in JavaScript. React's performance can be affected by blocking the event loop with heavy computations.

// ❌ Blocking the event loop
function HeavyComponent() {
    useEffect(() => {
        // This blocks the event loop
        const result = heavyComputation();
        setData(result);
    }, []);
}

// ✅ Using web workers or splitting
function HeavyComponent() {
    useEffect(() => {
        // Use requestIdleCallback or split computation
        const performComputation = () => {
            const result = heavyComputation();
            setData(result);
        };

        // Schedule when idle
        requestIdleCallback(performComputation);
    }, []);
}

Q: How do you handle memory leaks in React applications?

Answer: Memory leaks occur when resources aren't properly cleaned up. Solutions include: 1. Cleanup in useEffect return 2. Proper subscription management 3. Avoiding stale closures 4. Using AbortController for fetch 5. Proper handling of DOM references

function useResourceCleanup() {
    useEffect(() => {
        const subscription = subscribe();
        const timer = setTimeout(() => {}, 1000);

        return () => {
            subscription.unsubscribe();
            clearTimeout(timer);
            // Clean up DOM refs
            if (ref.current) {
                ref.current.removeEventListener();
            }
        };
    }, []);
}

03

HTML Required for React

3.1 Introduction to HTML for React Developers

Simple Explanation

HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the skeleton of every webpage. In React, you'll write HTML-like code called JSX that gets transformed into real HTML. Understanding HTML thoroughly is essential because React components ultimately render HTML elements in the browser.

Think of HTML as the structure of a house - the walls, doors, windows, and rooms. React helps you build these structures dynamically, but you still need to know what each building block does and how to use it properly.

Technical Explanation

HTML provides the structural foundation for web applications. In React, JSX is a syntax extension that allows you to write HTML-like code within JavaScript. This JSX gets compiled to React.createElement() calls, which produce virtual DOM elements that are eventually rendered as real HTML elements.

Key concepts for React developers: - Semantic HTML: Using appropriate elements for meaning - Accessibility: ARIA attributes and proper semantics - Forms: Controlled vs uncontrolled components - Events: Synthetic event system - Attributes: React-specific vs HTML attributes

Professional Explanation

In enterprise React development, HTML knowledge extends beyond basic markup. You need to understand:

  • Document Structure: DOCTYPE, meta tags, semantic elements
  • Accessibility: WCAG compliance, ARIA roles, keyboard navigation
  • SEO: Meta tags, semantic structure, Open Graph
  • Performance: Resource loading, prefetching, preloading
  • Security: CSP, XSS prevention, input sanitization
  • Internationalization: lang attributes, dir attributes
  • Progressive Enhancement: Graceful degradation

3.2 Document Structure

3.2.1 DOCTYPE and Basic Structure

<!-- HTML5 DOCTYPE -->
<!DOCTYPE html>

<!-- HTML Document Structure -->
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <!-- Character Encoding -->
    <meta charset="UTF-8">

    <!-- Viewport for Responsive Design -->
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">

    <!-- Page Title -->
    <title>My React Application</title>

    <!-- Meta Description for SEO -->
    <meta name="description" content="A professional React application">

    <!-- Favicon -->
    <link rel="icon" type="image/x-icon" href="/favicon.ico">

    <!-- Stylesheets -->
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/styles.css">

    <!-- Preconnect for Performance -->
    <link rel="preconnect" href="https://api.example.com">

    <!-- Preload Critical Resources -->
    <link rel="preload" href="/critical.css" as="style">

    <!-- Open Graph Meta Tags -->
    <meta property="og:title" content="My React App">
    <meta property="og:description" content="Professional React application">
    <meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/og-image.jpg">

    <!-- Theme Color -->
    <meta name="theme-color" content="#ffffff">
</head>
<body>
    <!-- React Mounting Point -->
    <div id="root"></div>

    <!-- Non-React Content (for SEO or fallback) -->
    <noscript>
        <div class="no-javascript">
            <h1>JavaScript is required</h1>
            <p>Please enable JavaScript to use this application.</p>
        </div>
    </noscript>

    <!-- Scripts -->
    <script src="/bundle.js"></script>
</body>
</html>

3.2.2 React Integration Points

// React mounting in index.js
import React from 'react';
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client';
import App from './App';
import './index.css';

// Get the root element from HTML
const rootElement = document.getElementById('root');

// Create React root and render
const root = ReactDOM.createRoot(rootElement);
root.render(
    <React.StrictMode>
        <App />
    </React.StrictMode>
);

// React component rendering to HTML
function App() {
    return (
        <html lang="en">
            <head>
                <title>React Application</title>
            </head>
            <body>
                <div id="root">
                    <h1>Hello World</h1>
                </div>
            </body>
        </html>
    );
}

3.3 Semantic HTML Elements

3.3.1 Structural Elements

<header> - Header Section

<!-- HTML -->
<header>
    <h1>My Website</h1>
    <nav>
        <ul>
            <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
            <li><a href="/about">About</a></li>
        </ul>
    </nav>
</header>

<!-- React Component -->
function Header() {
    return (
        <header className="site-header">
            <h1>My Website</h1>
            <nav>
                <ul>
                    <li><Link to="/">Home</Link></li>
                    <li><Link to="/about">About</Link></li>
                </ul>

        <li><a href="#services">Services</a></li>
        <li><a href="#contact">Contact</a></li>

</nav>

<!-- React Component -->
function Navigation({ links }) {

            <ul>

                    <li key={link.path}>

</main>

<!-- React Component -->

<section> - Content Section

<!-- HTML -->
<section aria-labelledby="features-title">

        </div>

</section>

function Features({ features }) {

        <section aria-labelledby="features-title">

                {features.map(feature => (

<ul>, <ol>, <li> - Lists

<!-- HTML -->
<!-- Unordered List -->
<ul>
    <li>First item</li>
    <li>Second item</li>
    <li>Third item</li>
</ul>

<!-- Ordered List -->
<ol>
    <li>First step</li>
    <li>Second step</li>
    <li>Third step</li>
</ol>

<!-- Nested List -->
<ul>
    <li>
        Category 1
        <ul>
            <li>Sub-item 1.1</li>
            <li>Sub-item 1.2</li>
        </ul>
    </li>
    <li>Category 2</li>
</ul>

<!-- React Component -->
function List({ items, ordered = false }) {
    const ListTag = ordered ? 'ol' : 'ul';

    return (
        <ListTag>
            {items.map(item => (
                <li key={item.id}>
                    {item.label}
                    {item.children && <List items={item.children} />}
                </li>
            ))}
        </ListTag>
    );
}

<img> - Images

<!-- React Component -->
function TextInput({ 
    label, 
    name, 
    type = 'text', 
    value, 
    onChange, 
    error, 
    ...props 
}) {
    return (
        <div className="form-group">
            {label && <label htmlFor={name}>{label}</label>}
            <input
                id={name}
                name={name}
                type={type}

                onChange={onChange}

                {...props}
            />
            {error && <span className="error-message">{error}</span>}
        </div>
    );
}

// Controlled Input with validation
function ControlledForm() {
    const [formData, setFormData] = useState({
        email: '',
        password: '',
        age: 18,
        terms: false
    });

    const [errors, setErrors] = useState({});

    const handleChange = (e) => {
        const { name, value, type, checked } = e.target;
        const val = type === 'checkbox' ? checked : value;

        setFormData(prev => ({
            ...prev,
            [name]: val
        }));

        // Validate on change
        validateField(name, val);
    };

    const validateField = (name, value) => {
        let error = '';
        switch (name) {
            case 'email':
                if (!value || !value.includes('@')) {
                    error = 'Valid email is required';
                }
                break;
            case 'password':
                if (value.length < 8) {
                    error = 'Password must be at least 8 characters';
                }
                break;
            // ... more validations
        }

        setErrors(prev => ({
            ...prev,
            [name]: error
        }));
    };

    return (
        <form>
            <TextInput
                label="Email"
                name="email"
                type="email"
                value={formData.email}
                onChange={handleChange}
                error={errors.email}
                placeholder="Enter email"
                required
            />
            <TextInput
                label="Password"
                name="password"
                type="password"
                value={formData.password}
                onChange={handleChange}
                error={errors.password}
                minLength={8}
            />
            <TextInput
                label="Age"
                name="age"
                type="number"
                value={formData.age}
                onChange={handleChange}
                min={0}
                max={150}
            />
            <div>
                <label>
                    <input
                        type="checkbox"
                        name="terms"
                        checked={formData.terms}
                        onChange={handleChange}
                    />
                    Accept Terms
                </label>
            </div>
        </form>
    );
}

<form> - Forms

<!-- HTML -->
<form action="/submit" method="POST" novalidate>
    <div class="form-group">
        <label for="name">Name:</label>
        <input type="text" id="name" name="name" required>
    </div>
    <div class="form-group">
        <label for="email">Email:</label>
        <input type="email" id="email" name="email" required>
    </div>
    <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>

<!-- React Component -->
function RegistrationForm() {
    const [formData, setFormData] = useState({
        name: '',
        email: '',
        password: ''
    });
    const [errors, setErrors] = useState({});
    const [isSubmitting, setIsSubmitting] = useState(false);

    const validate = (data) => {
        const errors = {};
        if (!data.name) errors.name = 'Name is required';
        if (!data.email) errors.email = 'Email is required';
        if (data.email && !data.email.includes('@')) {
            errors.email = 'Email is invalid';
        }
        if (data.password && data.password.length < 8) {
            errors.password = 'Password must be at least 8 characters';
        }
        return errors;
    };

    const handleChange = (e) => {
        const { name, value } = e.target;
        setFormData(prev => ({ ...prev, [name]: value }));

        // Clear error for field being typed
        if (errors[name]) {
            setErrors(prev => ({ ...prev, [name]: '' }));
        }
    };

    const handleSubmit = async (e) => {
        e.preventDefault();

        const validationErrors = validate(formData);
        if (Object.keys(validationErrors).length > 0) {
            setErrors(validationErrors);
            return;
        }

        setIsSubmitting(true);
        try {
            await submitForm(formData);
            // Handle success
            console.log('Form submitted successfully');
        } catch (error) {
            // Handle error
            setErrors({ submit: error.message });
        } finally {
            setIsSubmitting(false);
        }
    };

    return (
        <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} noValidate>
            <div className="form-group">
                <label htmlFor="name">Name:</label>
                <input
                    type="text"
                    id="name"
                    name="name"
                    value={formData.name}
                    onChange={handleChange}
                    className={errors.name ? 'error' : ''}
                />
                {errors.name && (
                    <span className="error-message">{errors.name}</span>
                )}
            </div>

            <div className="form-group">
                <label htmlFor="email">Email:</label>
                <input
                    type="email"
                    id="email"
                    name="email"
                    value={formData.email}
                    onChange={handleChange}
                    className={errors.email ? 'error' : ''}
                />
                {errors.email && (
                    <span className="error-message">{errors.email}</span>
                )}
            </div>

            <div className="form-group">
                <label htmlFor="password">Password:</label>
                <input
                    type="password"
                    id="password"
                    name="password"
                    value={formData.password}
                    onChange={handleChange}
                    className={errors.password ? 'error' : ''}
                />
                {errors.password && (
                    <span className="error-message">{errors.password}</span>
                )}
            </div>

            {errors.submit && (
                <div className="error-message">{errors.submit}</div>
            )}

            <button type="submit" disabled={isSubmitting}>
                {isSubmitting ? 'Submitting...' : 'Register'}
            </button>
        </form>
    );
}

<!-- React Component -->
function DataTable({ 
    columns, 
    data, 
    caption,
    onRowClick,
    loading = false 
}) {
    if (loading) {
        return <div className="loading">Loading...</div>;
    }

    return (
        <table className="data-table">
            {caption && <caption>{caption}</caption>}
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    {columns.map(col => (
                        <th key={col.key}>{col.label}</th>
                    ))}
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                {data.map((row, index) => (
                    <tr 
                        key={row.id || index}
                        onClick={() => onRowClick?.(row)}
                        className={onRowClick ? 'clickable' : ''}
                    >
                        {columns.map(col => (
                            <td key={col.key}>
                                {col.render ? col.render(row[col.key], row) : row[col.key]}
                            </td>
                        ))}
                    </tr>
                ))}
            </tbody>
            <tfoot>
                <tr>
                    <td colSpan={columns.length}>
                        Total: {data.length} items
                    </td>
                </tr>
            </tfoot>
        </table>
    );
}

// Usage
function UserTable() {

                    {status}

    const data = [
        { id: 1, name: 'John Doe', email: 'john@example.com', status: 'Active' },
        { id: 2, name: 'Jane Smith', email: 'jane@example.com', status: 'Inactive' }
    ];

    const handleRowClick = (row) => {
        console.log('Selected:', row);
    };

    return (
        <DataTable
            columns={columns}
            data={data}
            caption="User Information"
            onRowClick={handleRowClick}
        />
    );
}

<!-- React Component -->
function Link({ 
    to, 
    children, 
    external = false, 
    className, 
    onClick 
}) {
    const props = { className };

    if (external) {
        props.href = to;
        props.target = '_blank';
        props.rel = 'noopener noreferrer';
    } else {
        props.href = to;
    }

    if (onClick) props.onClick = onClick;

    return <a {...props}>{children}</a>;
}

<canvas> - Dynamic Graphics

<!-- HTML -->
<canvas id="chart" width="400" height="300">
    Your browser doesn't support canvas.
</canvas>

<!-- React Component -->
function Chart({ data, type = 'bar' }) {
    const canvasRef = useRef(null);

    useEffect(() => {
        const canvas = canvasRef.current;
        const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');

        // Clear canvas
        ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);

        // Draw chart based on type
        if (type === 'bar') {
            drawBarChart(ctx, data, canvas);
        } else if (type === 'line') {
            drawLineChart(ctx, data, canvas);
        }
    }, [data, type]);

    const drawBarChart = (ctx, data, canvas) => {
        const barWidth = 60;
        const gap = 20;
        const startX = 50;
        const maxHeight = 200;

        data.forEach((item, index) => {
            const height = (item.value / Math.max(...data.map(d => d.value))) * maxHeight;
            const x = startX + (barWidth + gap) * index;
            const y = canvas.height - height - 50;

            ctx.fillStyle = item.color || '#3498db';
            ctx.fillRect(x, y, barWidth, height);

            // Add label
            ctx.fillStyle = '#333';
            ctx.font = '12px Arial';
            ctx.textAlign = 'center';
            ctx.fillText(item.label, x + barWidth / 2, canvas.height - 20);

            // Add value
            ctx.fillStyle = '#555';
            ctx.fillText(item.value, x + barWidth / 2, y - 10);
        });
    };

    return (
        <canvas 
            ref={canvasRef}
            width={400}
            height={300}
            className="chart"
        >
            Your browser doesn't support canvas.
        </canvas>
    );
}

<dialog> - Modal Dialog

<!-- HTML -->
<dialog id="modal">
    <h2>Modal Title</h2>
    <p>Modal content goes here.</p>
    <button onclick="closeModal()">Close</button>
</dialog>

<!-- React Component -->
function Modal({ isOpen, onClose, title, children }) {
    const dialogRef = useRef(null);

    useEffect(() => {
        if (isOpen) {
            dialogRef.current.showModal();
        } else {
            dialogRef.current.close();
        }
    }, [isOpen]);

    // Close on backdrop click
    const handleBackdropClick = (e) => {
        if (e.target === e.currentTarget) {
            onClose();
        }
    };

    return (
        <dialog 
            ref={dialogRef}
            onClick={handleBackdropClick}
            className="modal"
        >
            <div className="modal-content">
                <header>
                    <h2>{title}</h2>
                    <button 
                        className="close-btn" 
                        onClick={onClose}
                        aria-label="Close dialog"
                    >
                        ×
                    </button>
                </header>
                <div className="modal-body">
                    {children}
                </div>
                <footer>
                    <button onClick={onClose}>Close</button>
                </footer>
            </div>
        </dialog>
    );
}

// Usage
function App() {
    const [modalOpen, setModalOpen] = useState(false);

    return (
        <div>
            <button onClick={() => setModalOpen(true)}>
                Open Modal
            </button>
            <Modal 
                isOpen={modalOpen}
                onClose={() => setModalOpen(false)}
                title="Welcome!"
            >
                <p>This is a modal dialog.</p>
                <p>It's accessible and uses the native HTML dialog element.</p>
            </Modal>
        </div>
    );
}

<!-- React Component -->
function ProgressBar({ value, max = 100, showLabel = true }) {
    const percentage = Math.min((value / max) * 100, 100);
    const isComplete = percentage >= 100;

    return (
        <div className="progress-container">
            <progress 
                value={value} 
                max={max}
                className={isComplete ? 'complete' : ''}
            >
                {percentage}%
            </progress>
            {showLabel && (
                <span className="progress-label">
                    {percentage.toFixed(1)}%
                </span>
            )}
        </div>
    );
}

// Usage in upload
function FileUpload() {
    const [progress, setProgress] = useState(0);
    const [uploading, setUploading] = useState(false);

    const handleUpload = async (file) => {
        setUploading(true);
        setProgress(0);

        // Simulate upload progress
        const interval = setInterval(() => {
            setProgress(prev => {
                const newProgress = prev + 10;
                if (newProgress >= 100) {
                    clearInterval(interval);
                    setUploading(false);
                }
                return Math.min(newProgress, 100);
            });
        }, 300);
    };

    return (
        <div>
            <input 
                type="file" 
                onChange={(e) => handleUpload(e.target.files[0])}
                disabled={uploading}
            />
            {uploading && <ProgressBar value={progress} />}
        </div>
    );
}

<meter> - Gauge/Meter

<!-- HTML -->
<meter value="70" min="0" max="100">70%</meter>
<meter value="0.6">60%</meter>

<!-- React Component -->
function Gauge({ value, min = 0, max = 100, label }) {
    const percentage = ((value - min) / (max - min)) * 100;

    const getColor = () => {
        if (percentage < 30) return '#e74c3c'; // Red
        if (percentage < 60) return '#f39c12'; // Yellow
        if (percentage < 80) return '#2ecc71'; // Green
        return '#27ae60'; // Dark green
    };

    return (
        <div className="gauge-container">
            {label && <label>{label}</label>}
            <meter 
                value={value} 
                min={min} 
                max={max}
                style={{ '--meter-color': getColor() }}
            >
                {percentage}%
            </meter>
            <span className="gauge-value">{value}</span>
        </div>
    );
}

// Usage in dashboard
function Dashboard() {
    const metrics = [
        { id: 1, label: 'CPU Usage', value: 72, min: 0, max: 100 },
        { id: 2, label: 'Memory', value: 45, min: 0, max: 100 },
        { id: 3, label: 'Disk Space', value: 88, min: 0, max: 100 }
    ];

    return (
        <div>
            {metrics.map(metric => (
                <Gauge
                    key={metric.id}
                    label={metric.label}
                    value={metric.value}
                    min={metric.min}
                    max={metric.max}
                />
            ))}
        </div>
    );
}

// ARIA attributes for accessibility
function AccessibleComponent({ isOpen, onClose, items }) {
    const [selectedIndex, setSelectedIndex] = useState(0);

    return (
        <div role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="dialog-title">
            <h2 id="dialog-title">Dialog Title</h2>

            <div role="tablist" aria-label="Tabs">
                {items.map((item, index) => (
                    <button
                        key={index}
                        role="tab"
                        aria-selected={selectedIndex === index}
                        aria-controls={`panel-${index}`}
                        id={`tab-${index}`}
                        onClick={() => setSelectedIndex(index)}
                    >
                        {item.label}
                    </button>
                ))}
            </div>

            <div
                role="tabpanel"
                id="panel-0"
                aria-labelledby="tab-0"
                hidden={selectedIndex !== 0}
            >
                {items[0].content}
            </div>

            <button
                aria-label="Close dialog"
                onClick={onClose}
            >
                Close
            </button>
        </div>
    );
}

3.5 Forms and Validation

3.5.1 Form Validation

// Advanced form validation with HTML5 attributes
function ValidatedForm() {
    const [formData, setFormData] = useState({
        username: '',
        email: '',
        password: '',
        confirmPassword: '',
        age: '',
        website: '',
        birthDate: ''
    });

    const [touched, setTouched] = useState({});
    const [errors, setErrors] = useState({});

    const validators = {
        username: (value) => {
            if (!value) return 'Username is required';
            if (value.length < 3) return 'Username must be at least 3 characters';
            if (!/^[a-zA-Z0-9_]+$/.test(value)) {
                return 'Username can only contain letters, numbers, and underscores';
            }
            return '';
        },
        email: (value) => {
            if (!value) return 'Email is required';
            if (!/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(value)) {
                return 'Please enter a valid email address';
            }
            return '';
        },
        password: (value) => {
            if (!value) return 'Password is required';
            if (value.length < 8) return 'Password must be at least 8 characters';
            if (!/[A-Z]/.test(value)) {
                return 'Password must contain at least one uppercase letter';
            }
            if (!/[a-z]/.test(value)) {
                return 'Password must contain at least one lowercase letter';
            }
            if (!/[0-9]/.test(value)) {
                return 'Password must contain at least one number';
            }
            if (!/[!@#$%^&*]/.test(value)) {
                return 'Password must contain at least one special character';
            }
            return '';
        },
        confirmPassword: (value) => {
            if (!value) return 'Please confirm your password';
            if (value !== formData.password) return 'Passwords do not match';
            return '';
        },
        age: (value) => {
            const num = Number(value);
            if (!value) return 'Age is required';
            if (isNaN(num)) return 'Please enter a valid number';
            if (num < 13) return 'You must be at least 13 years old';
            if (num > 120) return 'Please enter a valid age';
            return '';
        },
        website: (value) => {
            if (!value) return '';
            try {
                new URL(value);
                return '';
            } catch {
                return 'Please enter a valid URL';
            }
        },
        birthDate: (value) => {
            if (!value) return 'Birth date is required';
            const date = new Date(value);
            const today = new Date();
            let age = today.getFullYear() - date.getFullYear();
            const monthDiff = today.getMonth() - date.getMonth();
            if (monthDiff < 0 || (monthDiff === 0 && today.getDate() < date.getDate())) {
                age--;
            }
            if (age < 13) return 'You must be at least 13 years old';
            return '';
        }
    };

    const validate = (name, value) => {
        return validators[name] ? validators[name](value) : '';
    };

    const handleChange = (e) => {
        const { name, value, type, checked } = e.target;
        const val = type === 'checkbox' ? checked : value;

        setFormData(prev => ({ ...prev, [name]: val }));

        // Validate on change
        const error = validate(name, val);
        setErrors(prev => ({ ...prev, [name]: error }));
    };

    const handleBlur = (e) => {
        const { name } = e.target;
        setTouched(prev => ({ ...prev, [name]: true }));
    };

    const handleSubmit = (e) => {
        e.preventDefault();

        // Validate all fields
        const newErrors = {};
        Object.keys(validators).forEach(key => {
            const error = validate(key, formData[key]);
            if (error) newErrors[key] = error;
        });

        setErrors(newErrors);
        setTouched(Object.keys(formData).reduce((acc, key) => ({ ...acc, [key]: true }), {}));

        if (Object.keys(newErrors).length === 0) {
            // Form is valid
            console.log('Form submitted:', formData);
        }
    };

    return (
        <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} noValidate>
            <div className="form-group">
                <label htmlFor="username">
                    Username <span className="required">*</span>
                </label>
                <input
                    type="text"
                    id="username"
                    name="username"
                    value={formData.username}
                    onChange={handleChange}
                    onBlur={handleBlur}
                    className={touched.username && errors.username ? 'error' : ''}
                    aria-describedby={errors.username ? 'username-error' : undefined}
                    required
                    pattern="[a-zA-Z0-9_]{3,20}"
                    title="3-20 characters, letters, numbers, and underscores only"
                />
                {touched.username && errors.username && (
                    <span id="username-error" className="error-message" role="alert">
                        {errors.username}
                    </span>
                )}
            </div>

            <div className="form-group">
                <label htmlFor="email">Email <span className="required">*</span></label>
                <input
                    type="email"
                    id="email"
                    name="email"
                    value={formData.email}
                    onChange={handleChange}
                    onBlur={handleBlur}
                    className={touched.email && errors.email ? 'error' : ''}
                    required
                />
                {touched.email && errors.email && (
                    <span className="error-message">{errors.email}</span>
                )}
            </div>

            <div className="form-group">
                <label htmlFor="password">Password <span className="required">*</span></label>
                <input
                    type="password"
                    id="password"
                    name="password"
                    value={formData.password}
                    onChange={handleChange}
                    onBlur={handleBlur}
                    className={touched.password && errors.password ? 'error' : ''}
                    minLength={8}
                    required
                />
                <div className="password-strength">
                    <span className="strength-label">Password strength: </span>
                    <span className={`strength-${getPasswordStrength(formData.password)}`}>
                        {getPasswordStrength(formData.password)}
                    </span>
                </div>
                {touched.password && errors.password && (
                    <span className="error-message">{errors.password}</span>
                )}
            </div>

            <div className="form-group">
                <label htmlFor="confirmPassword">Confirm Password <span className="required">*</span></label>
                <input
                    type="password"
                    id="confirmPassword"
                    name="confirmPassword"
                    value={formData.confirmPassword}
                    onChange={handleChange}
                    onBlur={handleBlur}
                    className={touched.confirmPassword && errors.confirmPassword ? 'error' : ''}
                    required
                />
                {touched.confirmPassword && errors.confirmPassword && (
                    <span className="error-message">{errors.confirmPassword}</span>
                )}
            </div>

            <div className="form-group">
                <label htmlFor="age">Age <span className="required">*</span></label>
                <input
                    type="number"
                    id="age"
                    name="age"
                    value={formData.age}
                    onChange={handleChange}
                    onBlur={handleBlur}
                    className={touched.age && errors.age ? 'error' : ''}
                    min="13"
                    max="120"
                    required
                />
                {touched.age && errors.age && (
                    <span className="error-message">{errors.age}</span>
                )}
            </div>

            <div className="form-group">
                <label htmlFor="website">Website</label>
                <input
                    type="url"
                    id="website"
                    name="website"
                    value={formData.website}
                    onChange={handleChange}
                    onBlur={handleBlur}
                    className={touched.website && errors.website ? 'error' : ''}
                    placeholder="https://example.com"
                />
                {touched.website && errors.website && (
                    <span className="error-message">{errors.website}</span>
                )}
            </div>

            <div className="form-group">
                <label htmlFor="birthDate">Birth Date <span className="required">*</span></label>
                <input
                    type="date"
                    id="birthDate"
                    name="birthDate"
                    value={formData.birthDate}
                    onChange={handleChange}
                    onBlur={handleBlur}
                    className={touched.birthDate && errors.birthDate ? 'error' : ''}
                    required
                />
                {touched.birthDate && errors.birthDate && (
                    <span className="error-message">{errors.birthDate}</span>
                )}
            </div>

            <button type="submit">Submit</button>
        </form>
    );
}

// Password strength helper
function getPasswordStrength(password) {
    let score = 0;
    if (password.length >= 8) score++;
    if (/[A-Z]/.test(password)) score++;
    if (/[a-z]/.test(password)) score++;
    if (/[0-9]/.test(password)) score++;
    if (/[!@#$%^&*]/.test(password)) score++;

    switch (score) {
        case 0:
        case 1: return 'weak';
        case 2:
        case 3: return 'medium';
        case 4:
        case 5: return 'strong';
        default: return 'weak';
    }
}

3.6.2 ARIA Implementation

// Comprehensive ARIA implementation
function AccessibleMenu({ items, onSelect }) {
    const [activeIndex, setActiveIndex] = useState(0);
    const menuRef = useRef(null);

    useEffect(() => {
        if (menuRef.current) {
            const firstItem = menuRef.current.querySelector('[role="menuitem"]');
            if (firstItem) {
                firstItem.focus();
            }
        }
    }, []);

    const handleKeyDown = (e) => {
        let newIndex = activeIndex;
        switch (e.key) {
            case 'ArrowDown':
                e.preventDefault();
                newIndex = (activeIndex + 1) % items.length;
                break;
            case 'ArrowUp':
                e.preventDefault();
                newIndex = (activeIndex - 1 + items.length) % items.length;
                break;
            case 'Home':
                e.preventDefault();
                newIndex = 0;
                break;
            case 'End':
                e.preventDefault();
                newIndex = items.length - 1;
                break;
            case 'Enter':
            case ' ':
                e.preventDefault();
                onSelect(items[activeIndex]);
                break;
            default:
                return;
        }

        setActiveIndex(newIndex);
        const menuItems = menuRef.current.querySelectorAll('[role="menuitem"]');
        menuItems[newIndex]?.focus();
    };

    return (
        <div
            ref={menuRef}
            role="menu"
            aria-label="Navigation menu"
            onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}
        >
            {items.map((item, index) => (
                <div
                    key={item.id}
                    role="menuitem"
                    tabIndex={index === activeIndex ? 0 : -1}
                    aria-current={index === activeIndex ? 'true' : 'false'}
                    onClick={() => onSelect(item)}
                    onMouseEnter={() => setActiveIndex(index)}
                    className={`menu-item ${index === activeIndex ? 'active' : ''}`}
                >
                    {item.icon && <span aria-hidden="true">{item.icon}</span>}
                    {item.label}
                    {item.shortcut && (
                        <span className="shortcut">{item.shortcut}</span>
                    )}
                </div>
            ))}
        </div>
    );
}

// SEO component with React Helmet
import { Helmet } from 'react-helmet';

function SEO({ 
    title, 
    description, 
    keywords, 
    image, 
    url, 
    type = 'website',
    author = 'Your Company'
}) {
    return (
        <Helmet>
            {/* Basic Meta Tags */}

            <meta name="description" content={description} />
            <meta name="keywords" content={keywords} />
            <meta name="author" content={author} />

            {/* Open Graph Meta Tags */}

            <meta property="og:description" content={description} />
            <meta property="og:image" content={image} />
            <meta property="og:url" content={url} />
            <meta property="og:type" content={type} />

            {/* Twitter Card */}
            <meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
            <meta name="twitter:title" content={title} />
            <meta name="twitter:description" content={description} />
            <meta name="twitter:image" content={image} />

            {/* JSON-LD Structured Data */}
            <script type="application/ld+json">
                {JSON.stringify({
                    '@context': 'https://schema.org',
                    '@type': 'WebPage',
                    'name': title,
                    'description': description,
                    'url': url,
                    'author': {
                        '@type': 'Organization',
                        'name': author
                    }
                })}
            </script>
        </Helmet>
    );
}

3.7.2 Sitemaps and Robots

// Sitemap generation configuration
function generateSitemap() {
    const baseUrl = 'https://example.com';
    const routes = [
        { path: '/', priority: 1.0, changefreq: 'daily' },
        { path: '/about', priority: 0.8, changefreq: 'monthly' },
        { path: '/blog', priority: 0.9, changefreq: 'weekly' },
        { path: '/contact', priority: 0.7, changefreq: 'monthly' }
    ];

    const sitemap = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
    <urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
        ${routes.map(route => `
            <url>
                <loc>${baseUrl}${route.path}</loc>
                <lastmod>${new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]}</lastmod>
                <changefreq>${route.changefreq}</changefreq>
                <priority>${route.priority}</priority>
            </url>
        `).join('')}
    </urlset>`;

    return sitemap;
}

3.8.2 Progressive Enhancement

// Progressive enhancement in React
function ProgressiveComponent({ children, fallback }) {
    const [isSupported, setIsSupported] = useState(true);

    useEffect(() => {
        // Check if feature is supported
        const supportsFeature = 'IntersectionObserver' in window;
        setIsSupported(supportsFeature);
    }, []);

    if (!isSupported) {
        return fallback || <div>Browser not supported</div>;
    }

    return children;
}

// Component with progressive enhancement
function EnhancedFeature() {
    return (
        <ProgressiveComponent 
            fallback={
                <div className="fallback">
                    <h3>Basic Version</h3>
                    <p>Your browser doesn't support this feature.</p>
                </div>
            }
        >
            <div className="enhanced">
                <h3>Enhanced Version</h3>
                <p>Using modern browser features for better experience.</p>
                <button 
                    ref={(ref) => {
                        if (ref && 'IntersectionObserver' in window) {
                            // Use IntersectionObserver
                        }
                    }}
                >
                    Enhanced Button
                </button>
            </div>
        </ProgressiveComponent>
    );
}

3.9.1 Common HTML Mistakes in React

// ❌ Incorrect HTML practices in React
function BadComponent() {
    return (
        <>
            {/* ❌ Div soup - too many unnecessary divs */}
            <div>
                <div>
                    <div>
                        <h1>Hello</h1>
                    </div>
                </div>
            </div>

            {/* ❌ Using inline styles over CSS */}
            <div style={{ color: 'red', fontSize: '16px' }}>
                Inline styles everywhere
            </div>

            {/* ❌ Non-semantic elements */}
            <div className="article">
                <div className="title">Title</div>
                <div className="content">Content</div>
            </div>

            {/* ❌ Missing alt text on images */}
            <img src="image.jpg" />

            {/* ❌ Missing form labels */}
            <input type="text" placeholder="Name" />

            {/* ❌ Improper heading hierarchy */}
            <h3>Section</h3>
            <h1>Subsection</h1>

}

// ✅ Correct HTML practices in React
function GoodComponent() {
    return (
        <>
            {/* ✅ Minimal, semantic structure */}

            </header>

            {/* ✅ CSS modules or styled-components */}

            </div>

            {/* ✅ Semantic elements */}
            <article>
                <h2>Title</h2>

            {/* ✅ Alt text on images */}
            <img 
                src="image.jpg"

            {/* ✅ Proper form labels */}
            <label htmlFor="name">Name</label>
            <input 
                type="text"

            {/* ✅ Proper heading hierarchy */}

        </>
    );
}

3.10 Interview Questions

Junior Level Questions

Q: What is the difference between <div> and <span>?

Answer: - <div> is a block-level element that creates a new line and takes full width - <span> is an inline element that stays in the line with other elements

<div class="container">
    This is a block element
</div>
<p>This is <span class="highlight">inline</span> text</p>

Mid Level Questions

Q: What are semantic HTML elements and why are they important?

Answer: Semantic HTML elements describe their meaning to both browsers and developers. They're important for: 1. Accessibility - Screen readers understand the structure 2. SEO - Search engines understand content hierarchy 3. Maintainability - Code is more readable 4. Developer experience - Clear intent of code

<!-- Non-semantic -->
<div class="header">Header</div>
<div class="nav">Navigation</div>
<div class="main">Content</div>

<!-- Semantic -->
<header>Header</header>
<nav>Navigation</nav>
<main>Content</main>

Senior Level Questions

Q: How do you handle accessibility in React applications?

Answer: 1. Use semantic HTML elements 2. Implement ARIA attributes properly 3. Ensure keyboard navigation 4. Manage focus programmatically 5. Provide proper labels for form elements 6. Use proper heading hierarchy 7. Implement proper roles for custom components

function AccessibleModal({ isOpen, onClose, title, children }) {
    const modalRef = useRef(null);

    useEffect(() => {
        if (isOpen) {
            // Focus trap
            modalRef.current?.focus();
            // Prevent background scroll
            document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden';
        }

        return () => {
            document.body.style.overflow = 'unset';
        };
    }, [isOpen]);

    if (!isOpen) return null;

    return (
        <div
            ref={modalRef}
            role="dialog"
            aria-modal="true"
            aria-labelledby="modal-title"
            className="modal-overlay"
            onClick={(e) => {
                if (e.target === e.currentTarget) onClose();
            }}
        >
            <div className="modal-content">
                <header>
                    <h2 id="modal-title">{title}</h2>
                    <button
                        onClick={onClose}
                        aria-label="Close dialog"
                        className="close-button"
                    >
                        ×
                    </button>
                </header>
                <div className="modal-body">
                    {children}
                </div>
                <footer>
                    <button onClick={onClose}>Close</button>
                </footer>
            </div>
        </div>
    );
}
